title: Min Woo Lee Withdraws in Delhi After Stomach Illness Triggers Back Spasms
excerpt: The Australian, who had praised butter chicken and made chaat days earlier, withdrew from the DP World India Championship — and did not blame any dish for his illness.
body:
• Australian golfer Min Woo Lee withdrew from the DP World India Championship in Delhi after a stomach illness triggered back spasms, having played five holes of his second round.
  • Lee had opened with a one-under-par 71 at Delhi Golf Club and was level par overall when he stopped.
  • Days earlier he had praised butter chicken and taken part in a chaat-making session — but he did not blame any dish or meal for his illness, and no source links the food to the withdrawal.
  • His stated priority now is recovery: getting back to 100% before his next event.

Min Woo Lee's first tournament in India ended early. The Australian withdrew from the DP World India Championship at Delhi Golf Club after a stomach illness triggered back spasms, cutting short a debut week in which he had enthusiastically explored Indian food — butter chicken, and a hands-on chaat-making session — before he ever completed his second round.

Lee announced the decision in an Instagram Story. According to EssentiallySports, he played five holes of his second round — pars on the first and third, bogeys on the second and fifth, and a birdie on the fourth — leaving him one over for the round and level par for the tournament when he stopped.

"Sad to say I've had to withdraw from the @dpwic. A stomach illness triggered some tough back spasms, and I'm just not able to compete this weekend."

— Min Woo Lee, in an Instagram Story

What Lee Actually Said — and Did Not Say

The food angle needs care. Lee did not blame butter chicken, chaat, or any other dish or meal for his illness. His statement identified only a stomach illness as the trigger for the back spasms and gave no cause for that illness. Heavy, in a second report of the withdrawal, made the same point: Lee did not blame any particular dish or meal, and no connection between the food he enjoyed and the illness has been confirmed.

That distinction matters because the sequence invites an easy assumption. A golfer praised local food on Tuesday and withdrew with a stomach illness later in the week. Sequence is not cause, and neither report — nor Lee himself — makes that link.

The Food He Came For

Before the tournament, Lee sounded like a visitor determined to eat well. At his October 14 press conference, he described starting gently with a familiar dish before working his way up.

"Yeah, I had butter chicken last night. It's not traditional, but I thought I would ease into it, start with something that I know and then work my way up. But it was unbelievable. It was really nice."

— Min Woo Lee, pre-tournament press conference, October 14

He also took part in a chaat-making session with chef Saransh Goila, and said the chaat he made, which had not looked promising during preparation, turned out "actually very, very nice." He was not alone in praising the food: Eugenio Chacarra said ahead of the championship, "I love the country, I love the people, I love the food," describing himself as "a big butter chicken and rice kind of guy." Rory McIlroy and Ben Griffin were also reported to have praised Indian food during the week.

Food is part of Lee's public identity. His "Let Him Cook" catchphrase and his nickname, "The Chef," follow him around tournaments, with fans wearing chef hats. Lee has said the nickname refers mainly to the shots he produces on the course — in a 2024 interview he admitted he rarely cooks at home, "once a year, probably." The chaat session in Delhi let him play the role literally, for once.

The Tournament He Leaves Behind

Lee had opened with a one-under-par 71, a solid start on a demanding Delhi Golf Club layout in a $4 million event running October 15-18. He was one of several players to leave the field early: Andy Sullivan also withdrew citing illness, while Grant Forrest and Anthony Quayle withdrew with injuries, according to the reports. Heavy also noted a difficult week at the course, including a prolonged thunderstorm that suspended play for five hours on the opening day.

Lee thanked DP World, the tournament staff and the fans for their hospitality and support, and said his priority now is getting back to 100%. For a player who arrived promising to work his way up the menu, the culinary tour of India remains unfinished. The golf, for this week, is over — and on the evidence available, the food is not the story of why.
